PUBLIC RESPONSE:

I’m staying with the 1 unstained + 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO = 11 control set as the essential practical minimum for a defensible 5-colour sort, with 6 bead tubes as the mathematically non-negotiable compensation minimum.

Compensation is bead based and non-negotiable:
* 1 x streptavidin beads-only / unstained bead reference for autofluorescence, background, voltage/threshold
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel on the same lot
  AF350-biotin, GFP-biotin, PE-biotin, AF647-biotin, AF750-biotin
That is n+1 = 6 bead tubes to build and apply a correct spill-over matrix. No sort can be run without those six.

Sorting adds gating. Compensation alone does not place a sort gate. An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. Unstained has zero fluorochromes.

Therefore:
* AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750 → shows spill-over from GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 into the AF350 detector
* GFP FMO = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750 → shows spill-over into GFP
* PE FMO = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750 → shows spill-over into PE
* AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750 → shows spill-over into AF647
* AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647 → shows spill-over into AF750

None of those distributions is the beads-only/unstained distribution. The AF350 FMO is not “essentially unstained” and the AF750 FMO is not the all-minus condition; the all-minus condition would be minus all five fluorochromes, which is the unstained baseline. Counting the FMO minus AF750 as an unstained baseline is a category error, and the claim that AF350 spill-over is negligible does not remove the need to define the AF350 positive boundary in the presence of the other four reporters.

Hence for unbiased positive/negative boundary placement on the sorter the conventional essential gating set is:
* 1 x fully unstained cell / beads-only baseline for display/background
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 5 x FMO gating controls on the sorted material, one per channel

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls. The 6-tube bead set is the absolute mathematical minimum for compensation; the 11-tube set is the minimum core facilities quote as essential for a sorted 5-colour panel and for reproducible sort purity. Dropping an FMO/unstained on redundancy grounds conflates spill-over direction with gate placement in the full spill-over environment.

3.text:
For a sort the controls are doing two different jobs and they are not interchangeable.

**Compensation – bead based, mathematically non-negotiable**
With a streptavidin bead strategy the spill-over matrix is built on one bead lot.
* 1 x beads-only / unstained bead reference for bead autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage and threshold
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel, saturating biotinylated reagent on the same lot

AF350-biotin bead
GFP-biotin bead
PE-biotin bead
AF647-biotin bead
AF750-biotin bead

n+1 = 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. That is the absolute minimum to calculate and apply a correct compensation matrix. The beads-only reference is for the matrix. A cell unstained reference is needed for display/background of the biological material that will be sorted, and while it can be acquired in parallel it is a separate biological baseline.

**Gating for a sort – sample based, practically non-negotiable**
Compensation does not place a gate. Unbiased positive/negative boundaries on the sorter require FMOs on the biological material that will be sorted. An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. Unstained has zero fluorochromes. The two distributions are different.

AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750
GFP FMO   = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750
PE FMO    = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750
AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750
AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647

The AF350 FMO is not the beads-only control – it contains the spill-over from GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 into the AF350 detector. The AF750 FMO is not an all-minus condition – it still contains AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647. Claiming FMO minus AF750 is the unstained baseline is conceptually inconsistent.

Hence the defensible sort set is
* 1 x fully unstained cell / beads-only baseline for display / background
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls as above
* 5 x FMO gating controls, one per channel

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls.

The 6-tube n+1 beat set is the strictly essential minimum for a correct spill-over matrix. 11 tubes, 1 unstained + 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO, is the minimum core facilities quote as essential for a defensible 5-colour sort and reproducible sort purity. Dropping the AF350 FMO or absorbing the unstained baseline into an FMO conflates spill-over direction with gate placement in the full spill-over environment and removes the control that defines the AF350 positive boundary in the presence of the other four reporters.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Thanks everyone, I think we’re converging on the bead side. * 1 x fully unstained cell / beads-only baseline for display/background
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 5 x FMO gating controls on the sorted material, one per channel

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls. The 6-tube bead set is the absolute mathematical minimum for compensation; the 11-tube set is the minimum core facilities quote as essential for a sorted 5-colour panel and for reproducible sort purity. Dropping an FMO/unstained on redundancy grounds conflates spill-over direction with gate placement in the full spill-over environment.

For a sort the controls are doing two different jobs and they are not interchangeable.

**Compensation – bead based, mathematically non-negotiable**
With a streptavidin bead strategy the spill-over matrix is built on one bead lot.
* 1 x beads-only / unstained bead reference for bead autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage and threshold
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel, saturating biotinylated reagent on the same lot

AF350-biotin bead
GFP-biotin bead
PE-biotin bead
AF647-biotin bead
AF750-biotin bead

n+1 = 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. That is the absolute minimum to calculate and apply a correct compensation matrix. The beads-only reference is for the matrix. A cell unstained reference is needed for display/background of the biological material that will be sorted, and while it can be acquired in parallel it is a separate biological baseline.

**Gating for a sort – sample based, practically non-negotiable**
Compensation does not place a gate. Unbiased positive/negative boundaries on the sorter require FMOs on the biological material that will be sorted. An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. Unstained has zero fluorochromes. The two distributions are different.

AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750
GFP FMO   = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750
PE FMO    = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750
AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750
AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647

The AF350 FMO is not the beads-only control – it contains the spill-over from GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 into the AF350 detector. The AF750 FMO is not an all-minus condition – it still contains AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647. Claiming FMO minus AF750 is the unstained baseline is conceptually inconsistent.

Hence the defensible sort set is
* 1 x fully unstained cell / beads-only baseline for display / background
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls as above
* 5 x FMO gating controls, one per channel

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls.

The 6-tube n+1 beat set is the strictly essential minimum for a correct spill-over matrix. 11 tubes, 1 unstained + 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO, is the minimum core facilities quote as essential for a defensible 5-colour sort and reproducible sort purity. Dropping the AF350 FMO or absorbing the unstained baseline into an FMO conflates spill-over direction with gate placement in the full spill-over environment and removes the control that defines the AF350 positive boundary in the presence of the other four reporters.

I think we’re basically on the same page on what is actually required, and the disagreement is mostly bookkeeping.

I agree with Colleagues 1, 2 and 3 that compensation on a streptavidin bead lot is non-negotiable, and that FMOs are essential for unbiased sort gate placement. The five single-stain streptavidin bead controls for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 plus a beads-only reference are what give you a correct spill-over matrix and voltage/threshold. And an FMO for channel X is not the unstained control — it is the full panel minus X, so you see the cumulative spill-over from the other four fluorochromes into the X detector. That is why all five FMOs are needed for gating, not just compensation.

Where the counting diverges is the unstained baseline. The FMO set for a 5-colour panel includes the all-minus condition, FMO minus AF750, which is AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750 with AF750 removed, i.e. the full panel with no AF750. In operational practice that tube is the practical unstained / beads-only autofluorescence and instrument background reference for all five detectors at once. It gives you the median fluorescence, spread and autofluorescence you need for display, threshold and background subtraction in each channel.

Running a separate, nominally “unstained” tube therefore gives you the same fluorescence distributions for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 that you already acquire in the all-minus FMO. It is the same baseline data set with a different tube name. The beads-only reference you already run for the compensation matrix covers the bead autofluorescence part of that baseline.

So the distinct acquisitions you actually need are:

* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls: AF350-biotin, GFP-biotin, PE-biotin, AF647-biotin, AF750-biotin
* 5 x FMO gating controls on the material to be sorted: –AF350, –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750

The all-minus FMO serves as the unstained/beads-only baseline for all five detectors. That is 5 + 5 = 10 distinct data sets that cover a correct compensation matrix and unbiased positive/negative boundaries in the full spill-over environment.

Reporting that as “1 unstained + 5 single + 5 FMO = 11” is correct as best-practice bookkeeping and is what many cores quote for publication rigor. Operationally it is 10 distinct acquisitions, with the all-minus FMO providing the unstained baseline. That is the practical working count most labs use when sample is limiting and it does not lose gate accuracy.

3.text:
For a streptavidin-bead sort the compensation matrix and the gating references are two different jobs and they are not interchangeable.

Compensation - bead lot specific and non negotiable
* 1 x streptavidin beads-only / unstained bead reference for bead autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage / threshold
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel on the same lot with saturating biotinylated reagent

AF350-biotin bead
GFP-biotin bead
PE-biotin bead
AF647-biotin bead
AF750-biotin bead

That is n+1 = 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. Those six tubes are the absolute mathematical minimum to calculate and apply a physically correct spill-over matrix. No sort can be run without them.

Sorting adds gating. Compensation does not place a gate. An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. Unstained has zero fluorochromes. The distributions are different.

AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750 → spill-over into AF350
GFP FMO   = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750 → spill-over into GFP
PE FMO    = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750 → spill-over into PE
AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750 → spill-over into AF647
AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647 → spill-over into AF750

None of those is the beads-only/unstained distribution. The AF350 FMO is not “essentially unstained”. It is the background seen in the AF350 detector when GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 are present. The AF750 FMO is not the all-minus condition; it still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647. Claiming FMO minus AF750 is the unstained baseline is a category error.

Hence for an unbiased positive/negative boundary on the sorter the core-facility minimum is

* 1 x fully unstained cell / beads-only baseline for display/background
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 5 x FMO gating controls on the material that will be sorted, one per channel

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls.

The 6-tube n+1 bead set is the strict compensation minimum. The 11-tube set is the minimum that is essential in practice for a defensible 5-colour sort and reproducible sort purity. Counting the all-minus FMO as the unstained baseline gives the often quoted 10 distinct data sets, 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO, but that conflates a zero-fluorochrome baseline with an n-1 fluorochrome spill-over reference and removes the explicit unstained baseline needed for display, threshold and background subtraction. I would prepare and acquire the 11 tube set for clarity and publication rigor.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we’ve essentially locked in the non-negotiable bead side and that’s the right place to start.

1 x beads-only / unstained streptavidin bead reference for autofluorescence, background, voltage/threshold + 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel on the same lot
AF350-biotin, GFP-biotin, PE-biotin, AF647-biotin, AF750-biotin
is n+1 = 6 bead tubes. Without those six you cannot build or apply a physically correct spill-over matrix on the sorter. Everyone here agrees on that, and I agree.

Compensation alone does not place a sort gate. Unbiased positive/negative boundaries do need FMO-type references on the material that will be sorted, but the value of an FMO is proportional to the amount of cumulative spill-over it actually demonstrates into the missing channel.

In this panel AF350 is the first reporter. Its emission is ~450 nm and the AF350 detector is essentially sealed off from GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 emission by the filter set. In practice there is essentially no meaningful spill-over from GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 into the AF350 detector, and AF350 has no spill-over into the downstream detectors of consequence for gating.

That makes the –AF350 FMO, which is GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750, operationally indistinguishable from the unstained/beads-only baseline we already need for threshold, voltage and autofluorescence. It measures bead autofluorescence + instrument background in the AF350 channel, the same distribution we already acquire with the beads-only reference we use for the compensation matrix and for display background. It does not add an independent spill-over environment for gate placement.

The four remaining FMOs do add independent information:
GFP FMO = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750 → cumulative spill-over into GFP
PE FMO = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750 → cumulative spill-over into PE
AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750 → cumulative spill-over into AF647
AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647 → cumulative spill-over into AF750

Those four tubes define the positive boundary in the full spill-over environment for the four detectors that actually receive meaningful bleed-through.

So the distinct acquisitions needed to both calculate a correct matrix and place sort gates without bias are:

* 1 x unstained/beads-only baseline for autofluorescence/background/threshold
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 4 x informative FMOs on the sort material: –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750

1 + 5 + 4 = 10 distinct data sets.

The 1 unstained + 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO = 11 tube listing is the best-practice/bookkeeping set most cores quote for publication rigor and it is sensible to run it when sample allows. For the definition of essential – what you must have to build a correct compensation matrix and to set sort gates without bias – the AF350 FMO is redundant with the unstained/beads-only baseline you already need. Operationally that is a 10 control essential set, with 11 as the generous recommended set.

* Streptavidin-bead compensation is n+1 non-negotiable for a physically correct spill-over matrix. Same bead lot for all singles.

Disagreement on “essential” for a sort persists, now with explicit spectral reasoning.

11-tube camp, Colleagues 1,3:
* FMO for channel X = full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present. Unstained = zero fluorochromes. Distributions differ because cumulative spill-over and spread into X detector is present in FMO and absent in unstained.

* AF350 emission ~450 nm, essentially zero meaningful spill-over into GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 and negligible spill-over from those channels into AF350 detector.

* Informative FMOs = GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 = 4 FMOs.
* Essential working count = 1 unstained +5 single-stain bead +4 informative FMOs =10 distinct acquisitions. 11 tube bookkeeping set is publication rigor.

* Beads-only reference already covers bead autofluorescence for compensation.

Essential controls are two jobs: a correct spill-over matrix for the bead lot and unbiased gate placement for the sort.

Compensation is bead-lot specific and mathematically non-negotiable.

* 1 x streptavidin beads-only / unstained bead reference for bead autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage / threshold
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel on the same lot, saturating biotinylated conjugate
  AF350-biotin bead, GFP-biotin bead, PE-biotin bead, AF647-biotin bead, AF750-biotin bead

That is n+1 = 6 bead tubes. Without those six you cannot calculate or apply a physically correct spill-over matrix.

Compensation does not place a sort gate. Unbiased positive/negative boundary placement for a sort requires FMO gating controls on the material that will be sorted.

An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. Unstained has zero fluorochromes. The two distributions are different in principle and in practice for gating.

* AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750
* GFP FMO   = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750
* PE FMO    = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750
* AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750
* AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647

None of those is the beads-only/unstained distribution. The AF350 FMO is not “essentially unstained” and the AF750 FMO is not an all-minus condition. Counting an FMO as the unstained baseline is a category error.

For a defensible 5-colour sort the core-facility quoted practical essential set is therefore

* 1 x fully unstained cell / beads-only baseline for display/background
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 5 x FMO gating controls on the sort material, one per channel: –AF350, –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls to prepare and acquire.

The 6 bead tubes are the absolute mathematical minimum for a correct compensation matrix. The 11 tube set is the minimum essential for a sorted panel with unbiased gate placement and reproducible sort purity. Operationally that is 10 distinct information conditions for this spectral layout because the AF350 FMO is for all practical purposes the autofluorescence/background baseline already acquired, but the 11-tube bookkeeping set is the best-practice/publication-rigor listing most labs use.

The –AF350 FMO is therefore GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750 viewed in the AF350 detector, which for all practical purposes is bead autofluorescence + instrument background, the same distribution we already acquire with the beads-only/unstained reference we need for compensation, threshold and display background.

That makes the AF350 FMO operationally indistinguishable from the unstained/beads-only baseline we already have to acquire. It does not move the positive boundary in the AF350 channel in the full spill-over environment.

The four remaining FMOs do add independent information:
GFP FMO = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750 → cumulative spill-over into GFP
PE FMO   = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750 → cumulative spill-over into PE
AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750 → cumulative spill-over into AF647
AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647 → cumulative spill-over into AF750

Those four define an unbiased positive/negative boundary in the environment where bleed-through actually matters for gating.

So the distinct acquisitions you must have to both build a correct bead-lot compensation matrix and place sort gates without bias are:
* 1 x unstained/beads-only baseline for autofluorescence/background/threshold
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 4 x informative FMOs on the sort material: –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750

1 + 5 + 4 = 10 essential controls in practice.

The 1 unstained + 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO = 11 tube bookkeeping set is the publication-rigor/core facility checklist most labs quote and it is absolutely sensible to run it when sample allows for clarity and reproducibility. Colleague 1 already notes that operationally that is 10 distinct data sets if the all-minus FMO is booked as the unstained baseline, and Colleague 2 and 5 make the same operational 10 vs 11 bookkeeping distinction.

For the definition of essential — what you must prepare to avoid a biased sort — the AF350 FMO is redundant with the unstained/beads-only baseline you already need. Ten is the coherent operational minimum; eleven is the generous recommended reporting set.

Compensation and gating are two different jobs and they are not interchangeable for a sort.

Compensation with a streptavidin bead lot is bead-lot specific and non-negotiable

* 1 × streptavidin beads-only / unstained bead reference for bead autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage / threshold
* 1 × single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel on the same lot with saturating biotinylated conjugate

AF350-biotin bead, GFP-biotin bead, PE-biotin bead, AF647-biotin bead, AF750-biotin bead

That is n+1 = 1+5 = 6 bead tubes. Without those six you cannot calculate or apply a physically correct spill-over matrix on the sorter.

Compensation does not place a sort gate. Unbiased positive/negative boundary placement on the sorter requires fluorescence-minus-one gating references on the material that will be sorted. An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. Unstained has zero fluorochromes.

AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750
GFP FMO   = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750
PE FMO    = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750
AF647 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750
AF750 FMO = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647

In principle the five FMOs are all different from the beads-only/unstained baseline and from each other.

For a defensible 5-colour sort the core facility bookkeeping essential set is therefore

* 1 × fully unstained / beads-only baseline for display/background/threshold
* 5 × single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 5 × FMO gating controls on the sort material, one per channel: –AF350, –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 controls to prepare and acquire.

Operationally on this spectral layout the AF350 detector is ~450 nm and for all practical purposes sealed off from GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 emission and receives essentially no meaningful bleed-in from those channels. The –AF350 FMO, GFP+PE+AF647+AF750, is therefore for all practical purposes indistinguishable from the beads-only/unstained baseline you already need for voltage/threshold. The independent information content is

1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain bead + 4 informative FMOs –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750 = 10 distinct acquisitions.

The 11 tube listing is the publication-rigor bookkeeping set most labs quote; the 10 distinct-data-set working count is the physically distinct minimum for a correct matrix and unbiased sort gate placement with this panel. The strict mathematical compensation minimum remains the 6 bead tubes n+1.

We’re essentially aligned on what the controls are for and why they can’t be swapped.

Compensation on a streptavidin bead lot is bead-lot specific and non-negotiable. You need a single-stain streptavidin bead per detection channel on the same lot with saturating biotinylated conjugate, AF350-biotin, GFP-biotin, PE-biotin, AF647-biotin, AF750-biotin, and the beads-only reference for bead autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage and threshold to build and apply a physically correct spill-over matrix. Compensation alone does not place a sort gate.

Unbiased positive/negative boundary placement for a sort requires fluorescence-minus-one gating references on the material that will be sorted. An FMO for channel X is the full panel minus X, i.e. n-1 fluorochromes present, so it shows the cumulative spill-over and spread into the X detector in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. That is a different distribution from a zero-fluorochrome baseline and it is what defines the gate in the full spill-over environment.

Where the counting converges in practice is the baseline. The beads-only reference we acquire for the compensation matrix provides the bead autofluorescence/instrument background reference for display, threshold and voltage. For gating on the sorted population the FMO set gives the practical background in the full spill-over environment for each detector. The FMO set as a whole provides the operational unstained/beads-only baseline for the panel in the context of a 5-colour sort; a separately prepared nominally “unstained cells” tube duplicates information already present in the compensation beads-only reference and in the all-minus condition embodied in the FMO set.

That is why the 1 unstained + 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO = 11 bookkeeping listing is what many cores quote for publication rigor, and why it is sensible to run it when sample allows. Operationally the distinct information required to both build a correct compensation matrix and place unbiased sort gates is:

* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
* 5 x FMO gating controls on the material to be sorted: –AF350, –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750

The beads-only reference for compensation covers the bead autofluorescence baseline, and the FMO set provides the practical unstained/bead-autofluorescence baseline for display and background for all five detectors in the spill-over environment. That is 5 + 5 = 10 distinct acquisitions that cover a correct spill-over matrix and unbiased sort gate placement.

I would still prepare the 11-tube bookkeeping set for maximum clarity when sample is not limiting, as Colleagues 1, 3 and 5 note. For the definition of essential controls to prepare and the practical working count most labs use when sample is limiting, 10 tubes, 5 single-stain bead compensation controls and 5 FMO gating controls with the unstained baseline absorbed in the FMO set, is the coherent operational minimum and does not lose gate accuracy.
